boundary_decision.rationale: The registry-plane value standalone-mm does not identify the subject-model kind. The root owns a scheme release plus identity-dependent concepts, labels, relations, collections, mappings and change sets, so aggregate is more defensible than a single entity.

decisions.rationale: The scheme owns its governed concept graph and release history while classified objects, assignments, evidence, policy and search infrastructure remain external.
A classification binding normally points to a concept in a scheme, so parentage in the opposite direction may be navigational or reversed and cannot be approved from the frozen ledger.
Stable concept identity, definition and labels do not replace the person, place, product or other object classified by that concept.
Generic, instance, partitive and informal broader relations have different semantics; transitivity, cycles and polyhierarchy must be declared and validated per profile.
SKOS exactMatch, closeMatch, OWL sameAs, equivalentClass and registry mappings have different inferential consequences and never silently merge identity.
Language-tagged labels and typed notations are mutable designations; canonical concept URIs and authoritative identifiers remain the identity anchors.
Every structural change retains prior releases, successor mappings, impact on external bindings and resolvable identifiers rather than silently rewriting history.
SKOS, RDF, OWL, JSON-LD, MADS, DCMI, DCAT, DataCite and RO-Crate projections pin versions and disclose inference and round-trip loss.
Agents may append low-risk candidate mappings and checks but namespace creation, release approval, destructive change and protected disclosure require authority.

deferred_research: Resolve whether the WM-XCT-020 Classification Binding parent signal is navigational, reversed or should be replaced by an outbound reference from the binding to the scheme.
Develop domain-specific taxonomy, thesaurus, classification, ontology, multilingual, hierarchy, facet and mapping profiles.
Pin ISO 25964 replacements and every production crosswalk to exact releases and run bidirectional conformance, inference and semantic-loss tests.
Obtain independent terminology, library science, ontology, domain, accessibility, legal, privacy, security and records review.
publication_holds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet attempt timed out and one Grok attempt returned provider error 402 before producing an admissible result; no external result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-XCT-020 remains a reference because the registered parent direction appears navigational or reversed and requires joint boundary review.
Boundary hold: classified objects, classification bindings, evidence, organizations, policies, workflows, datasets and search indexes remain external masters.
Hierarchy hold: generic, instance, partitive and informal broader relations require explicit inference, cycle and polyhierarchy profiles.
Mapping hold: exactMatch, closeMatch, sameAs, equivalentClass and registry mapping semantics remain distinct and source-target versions must be pinned.
Language hold: multilingual labels require current BCP 47 registry validation, editorial policy and language-specific review.
Licensing hold: ISO and other licensed vocabulary profiles require legal review before reproducing protected structures or claiming conformance.
Interoperability hold: every standards projection requires exact release pins, conformance tests, round-trip tests and semantic-loss declarations.
Completeness hold: the 24-source draft is broad but does not claim universal domain, linguistic, ontological, legal or operational coverage.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
